question.leadin: Answer the following about Aaron Burr, (sir).
question.text: In his later life, Aaron Burr was involved in a bizarre plan to establish himself as the hereditary emperor of this country, America's southern neighbor.
question.clue: It's not Chile, but jaguar figures and colossal heads were made by this country's Olmec civilization.

swap.text: The Contras were from this Central American country.
swap.clue: In the 1990's, this country's rule passed from the FSLN to the opposition led by Violeta de Chamorro.

question.leadin: This man issued the Decree of War to the Death, condoning the murders of Spanish civilians who did not aid in his war of independence.
question.text: Name this man, known as "The Liberator" for his successful campaigns for independence in South America. A South American nation is named for him; one of its capitals is named for this man's compatriot, Antonio Jose de Sucre.
question.clue: This man's career followed that of The Precursor, Francisco de Miranda.

swap.leadin: The Mariel boatlift was a sharp increase in immigration from this country to the United States, which has utilized the "wet feet, dry feet" policy since 1995.
swap.text: Name this Caribbean nation, to which Elian Gonzalez was repatriated in 2000.
swap.clue: Operation Mongoose was a CIA program to assassinate a leader of this country using such items as a contaminated wet suit and poisoned cigar.

question.leadin: This South American example of state terrorism targeted Montoneros and Peronists.
question.text: The Montoneros conducted guerilla campaigns during this conflict, which saw the abduction and "forced disappearance" of dissidents and leftists.
question.clue: This campaign was rolled back under Reynaldo Bignone and was ended when the Radical Civic Union came to power.

swap.leadin: This man was imprisoned for a year on the Isle of Youth.
swap.text: Name this revolutionary, who led the 26th of July Movement to overthrow Fulgencio (fool-JEN-see-oh) Batista.
swap.clue: This man headed the 26th of July Movement; earlier he delivered the History Will Absolve Me Speech following a failed raid on the Moncada Barracks.

question.leadin: During an uprising in this modern-day country, Charles Leclerc was forced to retreat due to a yellow fever epidemic.
question.text: Name this country, where an uprising began after Dutty Boukman ("DUH-tee BOOK-muhn") drank pig's blood. After gaining independence, a civil war called the War of the Knives broke out in this country.
question.clue: This country and the U.S. Still dispute who controls Navassa Island.

swap.leadin: Human rights abuses during this leader's rule were investigated in the Rettig Report.
swap.text: Name this leader who overthrew his predecessor in a coup at La Moneda Palace. This leader was advised by a group of free-market economists nicknamed the "Chicago Boys."
swap.clue: On his 60th birthday, the CIA launched Operation Condor to suppress left-wing movements in this man's nation and neighboring Argentina.

question.text: In 1888, the Law of the Free Womb was expanded by this terse declaration of Pedro that immediately ended Brazilian slavery.
question.clue: This 1888 law signed by Princess Isabel while her father Pedro II was outside of Brazil. It abolished slavery and agitated wealthy landlords in Minas Gerais ("meen-ah zher-ays"), who later backed an 1889 Republican coup.

swap.leadin: Alberto Korda took an iconic photograph of this man in a beret, seven years before he was killed in Bolivia.
swap.text: Name this Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary who helped Fidel Castro take over Cuba.
swap.answerHtml: Ernesto "Che" Guevara [or Ernesto Guevara de la Serna; prompt on "Che"]
swap.clue: He limited the size of his country's farms to 1000 acres as head of INRA, appointed by Fidel Castro.

question.leadin: Identify the following about a rebel group.
question.text: This Sandinista leader, who continues to be active in Nicaraguan politics, was president from 1984 until 1990 when he was defeated by Violeta Barrios de Chamorro.
question.clue: In 1990, Pedro Chamorro's widow Violetta defeated this Sandanista ruler in the first free presidential elections in over fifty years.

swap.text: Jose Napoleon Duarte presided throughout much of a twelve-year civil war in this Central American country. In this country, the politically active Archbishop Oscar Romero was killed at the altar.
swap.answerHtml: Republic of El Salvador [or Republica de El Salvador]
swap.clue: The killing of Rutilio Grande in this country prompted liberation theologian, Archbishop Oscar Romero, to refuse to attend state occasions.

question.text: This leader ordered a failed assassination against Romulo Betancourt ("BET-ahn-coor"), Venezuela's president. This leader ordered the assassination of the Mirabal Sisters.
question.clue: The novel Feast of the Goat by Mario Vargas Llosa describes the end of this man's reign, as well as his abuse of the wives of his advisors, and after his assassination Joaquin Balaguer was placed in power.

swap.leadin: Troops kidnapped victims and drowned them at the port of Montecristi during this event.
swap.text: Name this 1937 event where tens of thousands were killed near the border of the Dominican Republic. Rafael Trujillo carried out this event named for a shibboleth that, if pronounced wrong, would result in execution.
swap.clue: This event was followed the next year by a campaign called "el desalojo," or "the eviction," which forced thousands to flee from the Cibao region.

question.text: While visiting these islands, William Dampier ate some native tortoises, which isn't surprising as he was one of the first people to use the word barbecue in a written English sentence. Charles Darwin later visited these islands and studied some of their finches.
question.clue: Isabela, San Cristobal, and Santa Cruz belong to this scientifically significant island group 650 miles off the western coast of Ecuador, also known as the Colon Archipelago.

swap.text: Santos has been criticized for not taking Uribe's side in his May 2013 war of words with this president of Venezuela, who was elected after serving as Hugo Chavez's vice president.
swap.clue: To date, Diaz-Canel's travels have taken him to Venezuela, where he has befriended this man, who has been running the nation as acting president after the death of Hugo Chavez.

question.leadin: This founder of the short-lived National Revolutionary Left Union delivered a speech called the "Oration for Peace" months before he was shot dead in the street by Juan Sierra.
question.text: Name this popular socialist politician who supported the radical agrarian reform called Law 200, and whose assassination in 1948 set off massive riots.

swap.leadin: The second part of this battle, fought at a namesake bridge, was preceded by a surprise attack at Gameza and the subsequent taking of Tunja.
swap.text: Identify this August 7th, 1819 battle that marked the final defeat of Spanish troops in New Grenada.
swap.clue: This 1819 victory for forces under Simon Bolivar consisting of Colombians, Venezuelans, and the British Legions resulted in the creation of the state of Gran Colombia.

question.leadin: While most famous for being named prima ballerina assoluta of the Royal Ballet, Dame Margot Fonteyn was also arrested in 1959 for smuggling arms by yacht with her husband, a member of this family.
question.text: Name this Panamanian political family, whose aforementioned member, the paraplegic "Tito,"was the son of Harmodio. This family's most famous member was Arnulfo, a three-time president deposed in three separate coups.
question.answerHtml: Arias family [or Roberto Emilio Arias, Harmodio Arias Madrid, or Arnulfo Arias Madrid]

swap.leadin: This man's rule is occasionally referred to as the second "Infamous Decade."
swap.text: Name this man with glorious sideburns who privatized the YPF as part of his Convertibility Plan as president of Argentina during the 1990s.
swap.clue: This Federal Peronist president during whose term Alfredo Yabran killed himself after ordering a hit on journalist Jose Luis Cabezas. This Syrian-Argentine president of the 1990s illegally sold arms to Croatia.
